# A reload recreate leaves the dock's tab body naming a destroyed pane

## Context

`test/playwright/e2e/dashboard/DockReloadActionNL.spec.mjs:74` fails in CI with the same page error on `dev` pushes and on unrelated PRs:

```
util.VNode.getVnode: Component not found for id: neo-dock-pane-2
    at VNode.getVnode (src/util/VNode.mjs:241)
    at VNode.createMap (src/util/VNode.mjs:25)   ← six levels of createMap
    at MainContainer.syncVnodeTree (src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:1293)
    at MainContainer.executeVdomUpdate (src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:571)
```

- **Failed on `dev` pushes:** `3c9ef1039f` (run 43629337258), `d6e427e7a7` (run 43652167453), `6f1f8b2df9` (run 43655757134). Passed at `c78adac361` (run 43662768030).
- **Failed on PRs whose diffs touch neither the dock nor its example:** `#20984` (twice), `#20989`, `#20910`.
- **Onset (inferred from CI history, not bisected):** the error first appears at `3c9ef1039f`, the merge of `#20961` ("an activation reconciles in place instead of rebuilding the shell"). It shows in 0 of 8 runs before that commit, and in 12 of 24 runs after it, 5 of which failed. In the other 7 it printed after the `workerErrors` fixture's check (`test/playwright/fixtures.mjs:260`), so the spec passed.
- **Local (measured):** at 1× CPU the spec passes 6 of 6. With CDP CPU throttling the error appears on `dev` (4× throttle: fails 2 of 5; 6×: fails 4 of 5).

## The Problem

The reload action recreates a pane that has no `dockReload()` contract. After that recreate, one live component's stored vnode still names the destroyed pane by `{componentId}`. Any ancestor flight that lands in that window throws while it maps the tree, and the workspace update fails.

1. **The recreate skips the unlink.** `commitRecreateCandidate` inserts the new pane, detaches the old one with `container.removeAt(index + 1, false)`, then calls `livePane.destroy()`. The detach clears `parentId`, so `destroy()` finds no parent and skips the unlink that `Abstract#destroy` performs for a pane that still has one.
2. **The container is mid-render.** In every failing run the main-tabs `Neo.tab.BodyContainer` (`neo-container-4`) is already mid-render (`isVdomUpdating: true`) when the recreate lands. So the update that `insert`/`removeAt` request is queued, and its `_vnode` keeps `{componentId: 'neo-dock-pane-2'}` until that update lands. In the 5 passing runs at 1× it was not mid-render.
3. **A workspace flight walks into it.** A flight of `neo-dock-workspace-1` that started before the recreate lands 1–9 ms after it. `syncVnodeTree` first runs `unlinkRetiredReferences(me.vnode)`, which by design walks only the root's own inline nodes. Then `createMap(me.vnode)` follows live references down to `neo-container-4` and throws on the dead one.

Why only since `#20961` (inferred): an activation now reconciles in place, so the tab BodyContainer survives the Swarm tab press. It can then still be mid-render when the spec clicks reload right after that press.

## The Architectural Reality

Anchors at `dev` `c78adac361`:

- `src/dashboard/dock/plugin/HeaderActions.mjs:732` `container.removeAt(index + 1, false)`, then `:736` `livePane.destroy()`. The comments make insert-then-remove-then-destroy the contract: "the predecessor must outlive its own removal".
- `src/container/Base.mjs:989` the default `removeAt` destroys with `item.destroy(true, silent)` while `parentId` is still set; `:996` the `destroyItem === false` path sets `parentId: null`.
- `src/component/Abstract.mjs:400` `updateParentVdom && parent?.vnode && VNodeUtil.unlinkRetiredReferences(parent.vnode, {[id]: vnode})`.
- `src/mixin/VdomLifecycle.mjs:1291` the root-level unlink (`#18321`), then `:1293` `VNodeUtil.createMap(me.vnode)`.
- `src/util/VNode.mjs:24` `createMap` resolves every `{componentId}` through `getVnode`, which throws at `:241` for an unregistered id. `unlinkRetiredReferences` (`:60`) keeps live references and does not follow them.

This is the only place in `src` that detaches a component with `removeAt(…, false)` and then destroys it. The other four callers (`LivePreview.mjs:542`, `:572`, `Reconciler.mjs:1238`, `VesselEmbodiment.mjs:201`) move live items.

Design authority: `src/util/VNode.mjs:54`, "a live reference is kept, never followed, since the stored vnode behind it is that component's own to keep clean", and `src/component/Abstract.mjs:398`, "The parent's stored vnode must stop naming a component the registry no longer knows".

## The Fix

In `HeaderActions#commitRecreateCandidate`, keep the order and unlink the destroyed predecessor from the container's stored vnode, as `Abstract#destroy` does for a pane that still has a parent:

```js
container.removeAt(index + 1, false);

const {id, vnode} = livePane;

livePane.destroy();
container.vnode && VNodeUtil.unlinkRetiredReferences(container.vnode, {[id]: vnode});
```

`VNodeUtil` is `src/util/VNode.mjs`. Measured as an App Worker hot patch on `dev` at 6× throttle: the fix failed 0 of 20 runs (10 plain, 10 with a 2 s settle), while a verbatim copy of the current method, hot-patched the same way as a control, failed 13 of 15.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After `commitRecreateCandidate` commits, the container's stored vnode no longer names the destroyed predecessor, including while the container's own update is still in flight.
- [ ] A deterministic regression spec (no timing) commits a recreate while the container is mid-update and asserts that mapping the tree from an ancestor does not throw. It is red on `dev` and green with the fix.
- [ ] `DockReloadActionNL.spec.mjs` passes every run under 6× CPU throttling locally, and `e2e-engine` is green on the PR.

## Out of Scope

- Letting `createMap` or `syncVnodeTree` tolerate dead references inside live descendants' stored vnodes. That is an engine-wide design call that hides real defects; the strict walkers are deliberate (`VNode.mjs:52`).
- The `CardGridContainment.spec.mjs:181` toolbar-sync flake, which fails on `dev` too (separate defect-note).

## Avoided Traps

- **`removeAt(index + 1, true)`:** it would destroy inside the removal and break the documented order, under which a failure leaves a live pane in the slot.
- **Re-running until green:** the error lands before or after the fixture's check depending on timing, so a green run proves nothing.
